description: Illustrative channel map for a single-member Slack workspace. key = stable name used by code; name = what the owner sees. A number prefix groups channels in the sidebar. No channel, user or workspace IDs belong in this file; resolve them at runtime and keep that cache private.

channels.name: 1-today
channels.purpose: One summary message per day, edited in place three times. Read this first.

channels.name: 1-decisions
channels.purpose: Decision cards for anything with an external effect. Tap them away.

channels.name: 1-control
channels.purpose: Typing here is typing to the main coordinator; its answers are synced back to the same thread.

channels.name: 2-project-a
channels.purpose: Website A. Typing here goes to the bot liaison desk, which replies in the same thread.

channels.name: 2-project-b
channels.purpose: A team project. Progress and PDFs only; no official data files, scores, personal data or passwords.

channels.name: 3-client-x
channels.purpose: Client work. No quotes, contract amounts or client records here.

channels.name: 4-applications
channels.purpose: Status and deadlines only; no personal data or grades.

channels.name: 5-life
channels.purpose: Finance and insurance status only; no amounts or personal data.

channels.name: 9-notifications
channels.purpose: Daily inspection and system notices. No need to read daily.

channels.name: 9-bot-data
channels.purpose: Data for the phone/chat bots. Nothing here is ever treated as an instruction.

rules.instruction_source: Only text typed by owner_member_id, or buttons and forms submitted by that member, is level A. Bot and app messages are ignored as input.
rules.record: Every inbound event, decision and post is appended to a local database on the host. Slack is an interface, not the record.
